title: Undo logging
description: Undo logging. Before-images in the undo log let the engine roll back uncommitted changes on abort or crash. InnoDB keeps undo in undo segments; Postgres keeps old row versions in the heap. Recovery scans for loser transactions and undoes them during startup.

title: Shadow paging
description: Shadow paging. Copy-on-write pages with an atomic root-pointer flip make commit a single pointer swap. LMDB and CouchDB use variants of this elegant scheme. The cost is fragmentation and copy overhead on every write.

title: The commit point
description: The commit point. Every atomicity scheme has one indivisible action: WAL flush, root flip, or consensus decision. Everything before it is undoable; everything after is durable. Design recovery around identifying exactly this point.
definition: The commit point — Every atomicity scheme has one indivisible action: WAL flush, root flip, or consensus decision.
key_points: Every atomicity scheme has one indivisible action: WAL flush, root flip, or consensus decision.
Everything before it is undoable; everything after is durable.
Design recovery around identifying exactly this point.
MVCC lets readers avoid blocking writers; it's the modern default.
Write-ahead logging orders log before data; violating it corrupts.

title: Crash mid-transaction
description: Crash mid-transaction. A crash between first write and commit must leave zero visible trace. Recovery replays the log forward to the commit point, then undoes losers. Idempotent replay matters because recovery itself can crash.
